title: EATF Action Evidence Package toolkit
description: Open toolkit for creating, inspecting, and offline-verifying Action Evidence Packages (.aep): a hybrid RSA-4096 plus ML-DSA-65 signer, two verifiers (TypeScript and Python), both built by Tyche Institute, sign/verify/inspect CLIs, RFC 9881 public-key encoding, JSON schemas, positive and negative conformance vectors, and a deterministic offline downgrade lab.
notes: Version 0.7.2 makes the two verifiers (TypeScript and Python, both built by Tyche Institute) parse a packaged pqc_public_key.pem by the same rules when no key pin is supplied. In v0.7.1 the Python verifier read an unpinned key with cryptography's PEM loader or a non-validating fallback, which accepted some key text the TypeScript verifier rejects, for example an SPKI PEM block followed by other text or the raw key as bare base64, and rejected some text it accepts (earlier versions crashed on those); with --pqc-signer-key the two already agreed. Python now uses the exact port of the TypeScript PEM parser that v0.7.0 added for pins. On differential corpora that are not part of this archive (34,522 generated signature and key entries and 5,088 PEM spellings), the two verifiers now return the same verdict and first-failure code in every case, with or without a key pin. The 5 accepted and 8 rejected conformance vectors, the 42 lab observations and the 21 decision-path cases give the same results as in v0.7.1. Previous version v0.7.1 is doi:10.5281/zenodo.23456866 under concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21763055; releases through v0.5.0 remain under earlier concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21511608.
